sources.entry: brotli - Python bindings for Google's Brotli compression library.

summary.one_liner: Google's Brotli, a generic lossless compression library and format (RFC 7932) with C reference code and Python bindings, listed in awesome-python under file manipulation.
summary.what_it_does: Brotli is a generic lossless compression algorithm combining an LZ77 variant, Huffman coding and second-order context modeling, and its format is specified in RFC 7932. The README describes it as similar in speed to deflate but with denser compression. It is a stream format with no built-in checksums or uncompressed length metadata. The README covers building and installing the library via Linux package managers, Homebrew, vcpkg, Bazel and CMake, and installing the Python module with pip. It links to compression benchmarks and lists related third-party projects such as an independent decoder by Mark Adler, a JavaScript port and a Dart FFI implementation.
use_cases: compress data for transfer or storage
add brotli compression to a Python project
build the brotli C library from source
install brotli via a package manager
notable: Implements RFC 7932 Brotli Compressed Data Format
Compression ratio comparable to the best general-purpose methods while staying similar in speed to deflate
Available through many package managers and build systems including vcpkg, Bazel and CMake
Related third-party decoders and ports in JavaScript, PHP, Python, Java, C# and Dart
caveats: Stream format with no checksums or uncompressed length metadata, so modified raw ranges of compressed data are not detected
The README does not describe the Python API in detail; it refers to a separate Python readme for source installs and testing
Related projects are third-party and the authors take no responsibility for them
